content:
According to reports, Apple's annual sales in India for the last fiscal year surpassed US$10 billion for the first time.

Given that the country's average annual income is less than US$3,000, this achievement is all the more remarkable, especially considering iPhones are sold in India at prices higher than in the US…

For years, iPhone sales in India were almost negligible for Apple. But in recent years, as the country's economy has developed and Apple has finally been able to open Apple Store locations locally, the situation has changed significantly.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given the low per capita income, and the fact that iPhones are now manufactured in India, you might expect local prices to be considerably lower than in the US. In reality, however, steep taxes have pushed Apple's pricing in India above US levels.

Apple has tried to offset this to some degree by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Currently about a quarter of iPhones are manufactured in India, though most of those are shipped to the US for sale. Apple restructured its logistics arrangements with the aim of sidestepping US tariffs on Chinese imports.
